key_insight: REST improves prediction of molecular information from H&E tissue images by weighting spatial-transcriptomics supervision according to its reliability.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support research into tumor heterogeneity and biomarker discovery, but clinical utility and drug-discovery impact remain unproven.
method: Organize curated gene signatures, pathways, and cell types into a Biological Program Bank.
Weight image–transcriptomics alignment using assay coverage and spot-level activity dispersion.
Use learnable biological-program queries to reconstruct gene expression from tissue morphology.
evidence_signal: Trained on 209 samples (407,475 spots; 16 organs) and evaluated on 70 disjoint samples (230,056 spots; eight organs), REST achieved the highest Macro correlation among compared ST-supervised methods and outperformed existing pathology foundation models.
watch_item: The abstract reports no effect sizes or prospective clinical validation, limiting assessment of practical benefit.
paper_title: REST: Reliability-Guided Spatial Transcriptomics Supervision for Gene Expression Prediction from Histopathological HE-Stained Images
